text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- CNPF employers' federation votes to support CFDT labour union chief Nicole Notat to manage unemployment fund Unedic.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe to seek parliamentary confidence vote on Wednesday.
-- President Jacques Chirac calls for a decentralisation of state administrative services, aimed at easing firms' relationships with the state.
-- Trading in Eurotunnel shares suspended pending statement on debt restructuring as mediators' mission came to end yesterday.
-- Cie Generale des Eaux deputy managing director Jean-Marc Espalioux may be the next Accor chairman, after joint leadership by Paul Dubrule and Gerard Pelisson.
-- Buying power of white-collar workers expected to stagnate in 1996, as taxes, contributions and inflation offset wage rises, study shows.

-- Renault carmaker Louis Schweitzer says possible buy by CGIP from Cerus of a 28 percent stake in auto parts maker Valeo would be an "excellent" move, expects 1997 French car registrations to reach 1.9 to 2 million vehicles.
-- Eurotunnel faces need to restructure a 69-billion-franc debt, analysts do not rule out a failure of debt-restructuring negotiations.
-- World Bank says need to adapt development aid to face changes in world economy that include a fall in state aid.
-- Mideast leaders head for emergency summit meeting in Washington on threats to peace process in the Middle East.
